use_case: AI assistant built into the ticketing and POS platform: (a) customer chat on the website and by text (hours, price ranges, booking, ticket status); (b) diagnostic suggestions to technicians from ticket symptoms and notes
vendor_or_model: Ticketing and POS vendor add-on (generative language model from an unnamed model provider acting as the vendor's subprocessor)
data_categories: Customer messages; ticket number, first name, and status; ticket symptoms and notes (which held passcodes and some account passwords); anything customers type (sample found passcodes and a card number)
consequential_decision_category: None (customer service and triage); escalates if it ever approves refunds or warranties, takes payment, or quotes without technician confirmation
human_in_the_loop: Staff take over on request and for complaints, refunds, off-list prices, batteries, and liquid damage; chat cannot change tickets or take payment; technician must inspect and confirm every diagnosis before a quote
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5, 15 U.S.C. 45(a)(1) and 45(n) (AI claim, AI disclosure, data use); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2) and (6) (chat and ticket data; vendor and model provider as third-party agents); PCI DSS v4.0.1 SAQ P2PE eligibility (card numbers typed into chat)
status: In production since 2026-05-04; chat approved with conditions due 2026-10-31; diagnostic suggestions suspended 2026-08-31

use_case: General-purpose public AI chatbots used by staff to draft replies, social posts, and repair write-ups, or to research faults
data_categories: Risk of customer details, device photos showing personal content, or passcodes being pasted
risk_tier: Low (High if customer data is entered)
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5, 15 U.S.C. 45(n); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2)
status: Allowed for general questions with no customer data; prohibited for customer data (POL-04 4.8; POL-02 C.8)
